title: Standalone components with explicit inputs
summary: Build a standalone product card that receives one typed product through an input.

scenario.briefing: The catalog page repeats the same card markup for every product. Extract a standalone card component, declare its product input, and format the price in the template.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Keep the @Component decorator and add standalone: true next to the selector.
Declare the input with @Input({ required: true }) and the Product type.
Interpolate product.name and product.price inside the template.
Call toFixed(2) on the price so every card shows two decimals.

misconceptions.description: Assigning to an @Input inside the child.
misconceptions.feedback: The parent owns the input value. Emit an output event or call a callback instead of writing to the property.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Writing to an @Input does not update the parent and Angular reports that the input is read-only in strict templates.

misconceptions.description: Declaring an optional input and rendering an empty card when the parent forgets it.
misconceptions.feedback: Make the input required so the compiler reports the missing binding before the page ships.
misconceptions.testDescription: The product input is required and typed.

misconceptions.description: Believing an input can be assigned to send data back to the parent.
misconceptions.feedback: An input is written by the parent binding. The child emits an output or calls a callback instead of assigning to it.

sections.title: A component owns one view
sections.body: An Angular component pairs a class with a template. The @Component decorator records the selector, the template, and whether the component is standalone.

sections.title: A selector places the component
sections.body: The selector names the element that instantiates the component. A parent template uses <app-product-card> and Angular creates the class behind it.

sections.title: Inputs are the public data contract
sections.body: An @Input property is written by the parent binding. Marking it required turns a missing binding into a compile-time error instead of an empty card.

vocabulary.definition: A class decorated with @Component that owns a template and its data.
A component that declares its own dependencies and can be imported without an NgModule.

steps.title: Render a product through an @Input
steps.prompt: Edit product-card.component.ts. Mark the component standalone, declare a required product input, and render the name and a two-decimal price.

tests.description: The component is standalone and keeps its selector.
The product input is required and typed.
The template renders the name and a two-decimal price.

hints: Replace the optional input with @Input({ required: true }) product!: Product.
Use {{ product.name }} and {{ product.price.toFixed(2) }} in the inline template.
Remove the TODO comment after the template renders both values.

steps.title: Component and input semantics

statements.label: The selector determines which element instantiates the component.
A standalone component can be imported directly by another component.
A child should assign to an @Input to send a value back to its parent.
A required input reports a missing parent binding at compile time.

steps.explanation: The decorator ties a class to a template and a selector. Inputs are read-only from the child's perspective: the parent owns the value, and the child renders it. A required input turns an incomplete call site into a compiler error.
hints: Check each statement against standalone component imports.
Reject the idea that a child writes back through an input.
Confirm when a required input fails the build.
Select only statements about selectors, standalone imports, and required inputs.
